title: MATH GAOKAO - 270
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a limit of the form \(\frac{\sin(kx)}{x}\) as \(x\to0\).
questions.question: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sin 5x}{x}\).
questions.explanation: Use the standard limit \(\lim_{u\to0}\frac{\sin u}{u}=1\). Rewrite \(\frac{\sin 5x}{x}=5\cdot \frac{\sin 5x}{5x}\). As \(x\to0\), \(5x\to0\), so the limit is \(5\cdot1=5\).
questions.hint: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(5\) to use the standard sine limit.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a trigonometric limit using the standard limit \(\frac{1-\cos t}{t^2}\to\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.question: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{1-\cos 4x}{x^2}\).
questions.explanation: Use \(\lim_{t\to0}\frac{1-\cos t}{t^2}=\frac{1}{2}\). Let \(t=4x\). Then \(\frac{1-\cos 4x}{x^2}=16\cdot\frac{1-\cos 4x}{(4x)^2}\). As \(x\to0\), \((4x)^2\to0\), so the limit is \(16\cdot\frac{1}{2}=8\).
questions.hint: Compare the expression with the standard limit \(\frac{1-\cos t}{t^2}\) by substituting \(t=4x\).

questions.concept: Trigonometric Limit with Tangent and Sine
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a limit involving \(\tan(ax)\) and \(\sin(bx)\) as \(x\to0\).
questions.question: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\tan 3x}{\sin 2x}\).
questions.explanation: Write \(\tan 3x=\frac{\sin 3x}{\cos 3x}\). Then \(\frac{\tan 3x}{\sin 2x}=\frac{\sin 3x}{3x}\cdot\frac{2x}{\sin 2x}\cdot\frac{3}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{\cos 3x}\). As \(x\to0\), \(\frac{\sin 3x}{3x}\to1\), \(\frac{2x}{\sin 2x}\to1\), and \(\frac{1}{\cos 3x}\to1\). Thus the limit is \(\frac{3}{2}\).
questions.hint: Express \(\tan 3x\) in terms of sine and cosine, then use standard sine limits.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a limit involving \(\sin(x^2)\), \(x\), and \(\tan x\).
questions.question: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x\tan x}\).
questions.explanation: Rewrite \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x\tan x}=\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x^2}\cdot\frac{x}{\tan x}\). As \(x\to0\), \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x^2}\to1\) because \(x^2\to0\), and \(\frac{x}{\tan x}\to1\). Therefore the limit is \(1\cdot1=1\).
questions.hint: Separate the expression into \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x^2}\) and \(\frac{x}{\tan x}\).

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a trigonometric limit by applying the sum-to-product identity for \(\cos A-\cos B\).
questions.question: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\cos 3x-\cos x}{x^2}\).
questions.explanation: Use \(\cos A-\cos B=-2\sin\frac{A+B}{2}\sin\frac{A-B}{2}\). Thus \(\cos 3x-\cos x=-2\sin 2x\sin x\). Then \(\frac{\cos 3x-\cos x}{x^2}=-2\cdot\frac{\sin 2x}{x}\cdot\frac{\sin x}{x}\). As \(x\to0\), \(\frac{\sin 2x}{x}\to2\) and \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\to1\). Hence the limit is \(-2\cdot2\cdot1=-4\).

questions.concept: Trigonometric Limit with a Radical Denominator
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a trigonometric limit by rationalizing a square-root denominator.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin 2x}{\sqrt{x+1}-1}\).
questions.explanation: Rationalize the denominator: \(\sqrt{x+1}-1=\frac{x}{\sqrt{x+1}+1}\). Then \(\frac{\sin 2x}{\sqrt{x+1}-1}=\frac{\sin 2x}{x}(\sqrt{x+1}+1)=2\cdot\frac{\sin 2x}{2x}\cdot(\sqrt{x+1}+1)\). As \(x\to0\), \(\frac{\sin 2x}{2x}\to1\) and \(\sqrt{x+1}+1\to2\). Therefore the limit is \(2\cdot1\cdot2=4\).
questions.hint: Rationalize the denominator or use \(\sqrt{x+1}-1\sim \frac{x}{2}\) as \(x\to0\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine a positive parameter so that a given trigonometric limit equals a specified value.
questions.question: Let \(a>0\). If \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{1-\cos(ax)}{x^2}=2\), find \(a\).
questions.explanation: Using \(\lim_{t\to0}\frac{1-\cos t}{t^2}=\frac{1}{2}\), with \(t=ax\), we get \(\frac{1-\cos(ax)}{x^2}=a^2\cdot\frac{1-\cos(ax)}{(ax)^2}\to \frac{a^2}{2}\). Setting \(\frac{a^2}{2}=2\) gives \(a^2=4\). Since \(a>0\), \(a=2\).
questions.hint: Use the standard limit \(\frac{1-\cos t}{t^2}\to\frac{1}{2}\) with \(t=ax\).

questions.concept: Limit of a Composite Sine Function
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin(\sin x)}{x}\) using the standard sine limit.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin(\sin x)}{x}\).
questions.explanation: Write \(\frac{\sin(\sin x)}{x}=\frac{\sin(\sin x)}{\sin x}\cdot\frac{\sin x}{x}\). As \(x\to0\), \(\sin x\to0\), so \(\frac{\sin(\sin x)}{\sin x}\to1\). Also \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\to1\). Therefore the limit is \(1\cdot1=1\).
questions.hint: Insert \(\sin x\) as an intermediate variable by writing the fraction as a product.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\tan x-\sin x}{x^3}\) using trigonometric identities and standard limits.
questions.question: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\tan x-\sin x}{x^3}\).
questions.explanation: Rewrite \(\tan x-\sin x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}-\sin x=\frac{\sin x(1-\cos x)}{\cos x}\). Thus \(\frac{\tan x-\sin x}{x^3}=\frac{\sin x}{x}\cdot\frac{1-\cos x}{x^2}\cdot\frac{1}{\cos x}\). As \(x\to0\), \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\to1\), \(\frac{1-\cos x}{x^2}\to\frac{1}{2}\), and \(\frac{1}{\cos x}\to1\). Therefore the limit is \(1\cdot\frac{1}{2}\cdot1=\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Factor out \(\sin x\) and use the standard limit for \(1-\cos x\).

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a cubic-order trigonometric limit using Taylor expansions of \(\sin x\) and \(\cos x\).
questions.question: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin x-x\cos x}{x^3}\).
questions.explanation: Use Taylor expansions: \(\sin x=x-\frac{x^3}{6}+O(x^5)\) and \(\cos x=1-\frac{x^2}{2}+O(x^4)\). Then \(x\cos x=x-\frac{x^3}{2}+O(x^5)\). Therefore \(\sin x-x\cos x=\left(x-\frac{x^3}{6}\right)-\left(x-\frac{x^3}{2}\right)+O(x^5)=\frac{x^3}{3}+O(x^5)\). Dividing by \(x^3\) and taking the limit gives \(\frac{1}{3}\).
questions.hint: Use Taylor expansions of \(\sin x\) and \(\cos x\) up to cubic terms.
